headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Chatwoot’s broad egress plus Marketingskills’ shared-context skills can move customer data into marketing outputs without strong verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can expose customer messages and reports, while marketingskills explicitly says skills “reference each other and build on shared context.” That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if Chatwoot content is copied into shared files or prompts. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into a shared skill file or prompt consumed by marketingskills
IF marketingskills treats imported context as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Separate Chatwoot exports from skill prompts
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data parser
Review any copied customer text before reuse
Disable shared-context chaining for untrusted inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and has broad network egress. Marketingskills reads and writes local skill files and can call GitHub and its own site. If customer content reaches those files or prompts, it can be transmitted outward or persisted in marketing artifacts, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF customer messages or orders from Chatwoot are placed into marketingskills skill files
IF marketingskills uploads or republishes those files through GitHub or marketing-skills.com
mitigations: Keep customer data out of shared skill directories
Use a redaction step before any export
Restrict outbound network access during review
Audit GitHub pushes for sensitive strings
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on file writes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad egress, and marketingskills can read/write files, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances. The pair can therefore contend over shared mutable artifacts if run in the same workspace, even though Chatwoot’s filesystem write capability is not documented. Uncertainty about Chatwoot’s local write surface pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF marketingskills instances run concurrently while writing shared skill files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes to shared files
Use read-only mounts for Chatwoot exports
Check in changes through one operator account
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marketingskills is designed so skills reference each other and build on shared context, which can cause Chatwoot-generated customer summaries to be reused as authoritative marketing input. Chatwoot can emit reports and messages, but there is no documented verification gate in marketingskills, so downstream amplification is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Chatwoot reports are fed into marketingskills as source material
IF marketingskills reuses that context without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before reuse
Mark Chatwoot outputs as untrusted source text
Add a checklist for factual claims
Limit marketing drafts to non-sensitive summaries
requires-engineering: add verification and citation checks

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while marketingskills is a marketing-content system with file and GitHub surfaces. If regulated customer data is copied into marketing artifacts or pushed to GitHub, retention and subject-rights handling can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so this is a compliance-process risk rather than a residency breach.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is exported from Chatwoot into marketing files
IF those files are retained or published outside the customer-support system
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from exports
Set a short retention window for drafts
Review GitHub commits for personal data
Document deletion/export handling for copied data
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
